- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) and forecast is significantly below recent highs, adjust upward by 1–2% to account for momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.3) and forecast is above recent lows, reduce by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If forecast shows a sharp spike followed by a steep drop, reduce the immediate post-spike values by 1–3% to avoid overshoot.  
- If forecast mean is consistently higher than true outcome over 10+ days, apply a 1–3% downward bias to future forecasts.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.6) and forecast deviates > 2% from true, apply mean reversion: adjust toward 3-day moving average of past 10 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently lower than forecast, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day for the next 5 days to reflect lagged market reaction.
